title: When Contextual Inference Fails: Cancelability in Interactive Instruction Following
abstract: arXiv:2603.19997v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We investigate the separation of literal interpretation from contextual inference in a collaborative block-building tasks, where an agent must resolve underspecified instructions using context. We adapt an existing two-speaker psycholinguistic paradigm into an interactive benchmark called Build What I Mean (BWIM). This setup contrasts a pragmatically cooperative speaker with one who is only literally reliable. In BWIM, models face underspecified instructions and must choose between making a contextual inference or requesting clarification at a small communication cost. Evaluating several state-of-the-art LLMs, we find a clear dissociation between judgment and action. Although models successfully detect speaker unreliability in explicit confidence ratings, they fail to leverage this awareness when taking action. Instead of deploying efficient clarification strategies, models default to suboptimal behaviors. These include partner-blind

translated_title: 当上下文推断失败时：交互式指令跟随中的可取消性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.19997v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：我们研究了在协作积木构建任务中，字面解释与上下文推断的分离，其中代理必须利用上下文解决不明确的指令。我们将现有的双说话者心理语言学范式改编为一个名为“Build What I Mean (BWIM)”的交互式基准测试。该设置对比了一个语用上合作的说话者与一个仅在字面上可靠的说话者。在BWIM中，模型面临不明确的指令，必须在进行上下文推断或请求澄清（以较小的通信成本）之间做出选择。通过评估几种最先进的LLM，我们发现判断与行动之间存在明显的分离。尽管模型在明确的信心评分中成功检测到说话者的不可靠性，但在采取行动时未能利用这种意识。模型没有采用高效的澄清策略，而是默认采用次优行为，包括无视伙伴的行为。
tldr: 该论文通过构建BWIM基准测试发现，即使大型语言模型能识别说话者不可靠性，在实际交互中仍无法将其转化为有效的澄清策略，导致上下文推断失败。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the BWIM benchmark and reveals that despite LLMs detecting speaker unreliability, they fail to translate this awareness into effective clarification strategies, leading to contextual inference failures in interactive tasks.
